featured_reviews.name: Vrushali Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been a regular customer here and have always enjoyed visiting, which is why this experience was particularly disappointing.

The staff member at the chaat counter was extremely rude. When I politely requested one extra masala puri, he abruptly replied, “Ho gaya,” in a very dismissive manner. I understand that I was asking for something extra, and I was even willing to pay for it. In fact, it was only after I offered additional money that he finally gave me the masala puri.

For a pani puri that is priced on the higher side, I expect at least basic courtesy and customer service, especially as a regular customer. It wasn’t about the extra puri it was about the rude attitude and the way the request was handled.

I hope the management addresses this and ensures customers are treated with respect.

featured_reviews.name: Shri Pednekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
All food items ordered were fresh, hot and delicious.
1) Dabeli was nice sweet and spicy with an ample amount of masala peanuts.
2) Veg toast sandwich - it's a triple layered sandwich. The amount of vegetables was perfect.
3) Paneer bread pakoda - it's an all time favourite having a big paneer slice stuffed inside.
4) Veg Pocket samosa - stuffing of samosa consists of cashews, raisins with potato masala.
5) Gulab Jamun - they are soft with cardamom. The size is pretty big.
6) Butterscotch shrikhand - different flavored shrikhand but definitely a must try.
7) Sandwich Halwa - it's thick in size unlike regular flat halwa. Consists of large amount of cashew nut, almond and pista.

featured_reviews.review_text: Love your bark butterscotch but had a bad  experience when my cousin ordered it for me via zomato. Firstly the bill was 1768inr and zomato charged me 1828inr. The delivery person was rude because he did not have change and it took me sometime to get change. I would sincerely suggest not to buy via zomato.

featured_reviews.name: Suhasini Sudan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Love their ambience, their decorations, and their trial sweet and savoury snacks. Love their unique twist on fusion Indo-western desserts and snacks. Their Avo Papdi chaat is delicious and so are their Gulab Jamun churros, their Rasgulla Tiramisu and their special strawberry menu. Their thick hot chocolate with the special cookie is also a personal favourite. I also love their chocolate barks, especially the strawberry chocolate one.

Has become such a stable, me and my friends go there practically every week. Amazing for a treat.

featured_reviews.name: Akarsh Kavuttan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally had the opportunity to visit the famous Bombay Sweet Shop!

Although I couldn’t have much as I had already ordered a bunch of sweets earlier on the occasion of Women’s Day!

Nevertheless the vibe was fantastic! The interiors were also fantastic!

featured_reviews.name: Priya pokhare
featured_reviews.review_text: Mithais are more than just good packaging and presentation. People may be all impressed with BSS but honestly I was a bit underwhelmed. I have gifted friends and family with their items . But they are overdoing the fusion stuff , which I guess is the point but they are losing their vision. I also think they do not use good quality chocolate for their brittle and fudge. The fudge tastes flat and nothing of chocolate. The only decent thing maybe the chocolate butter cookies . I would like to like them but they need to make it make sense for the price I pay .

featured_reviews.name: Anasuya Roshan
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had these delivered in Mumbai and brought over to Malaysia within 24hrs. They lasted the entire journey intact and lip smacking good!

I strongly recommend the Cheat Box, Assorted Mithai Box and Kalakand (any flavour of the Kalakand if you can get your hands on some). Bite-sized portions, provided you exercise control, which is impossible I'd say. Their namkeens are addictive, those should come with warning labels. All edibles are have allergens labelled on their packaging; it simplifies matters for those who have restrictive diets.

None of the sweets are overly sweet despite being 'sweets'. I'm not sure how to explain the irony of that sentence, but those who have an indulgent sweet tooth AND a hawk's eye on their calorie intake, you know what I mean.

Always a good experience shopping from you!

featured_reviews.name: Sassinator
featured_reviews.review_text: BSS is extraordinary!! We were introduced to the store thru an equally amazing 5 Senses Tour. We HAD to go back!! The service and the sweets were OFF THE CHARTS!! We even brought our Uber driver in to treat him to their delicious ice cream!!

featured_reviews.name: Amruta S
featured_reviews.review_text: Don’t buy from them online! I placed an online order in time for Diwali. The order was well Packaged but had an important missing item - the kaju katli burfi. Their customer service does not exist! Neither on WhatsApp, email or phone. Best to go to the store and get what you pay for instead of paying for missed items and chasing them with no result.

name: Brijwasi Sweets, Original Since 1946 - GD Group - Byculla
description:
In the early forties, a young man from Braj in Mathura, landed on the shores of the bustling metropolis called Mumbai. He arrived with a dream to have his own shop selling traditional mithais from his beloved Braj Bhoomi. While he established his first outlet in Kalbadevi, little did he know that he was in fact pioneering a leading chain of stores which would one day become a household name! This was our patriarch Ramswarup ji...

Subsequently, his son Bankelalji, and his succeeding present generations, have grown from strength to strength from that first outlet to several others across the city today. We continue to follow the age old traditional recipes to bring you the finest flavours in our products.

featured_reviews.name: Dr Amala
featured_reviews.review_text: This popular sweet cafe serves both desserts n savouries in unique combinations. We tried their panipuri with both avocado n aloo fillings n pav bhaji porter house rolls with amazing chaas butter along with mango + passion fruit lassi n gulab jamun. The quirky combination makes the delicacies mind blowing n a reason for repeated visits among locals. Must try their healthy treats as well.

featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text: We've been to Bombay sweet shop multiple times since their opening at phoenix palladium mall and always leave happy & content from their outlet. The staff are so sweet, warm. attentive,helpful and quick that really enriches our experience there. They have a laddoo game near the entrance which entertains the kids very much. There's also a soft serve given after crossing some cut off points in the game. It engages kids and adults alike,I must say. They have quite a few tables and hence the place is almost full. Luckily they serve really fast and we still got a table after a 10-15min wait time. Another positive is that it's open till midnight to stop by for a quick dessert too. We had tried their gulab jamun Churros, chilli cheese toast pav bhaji porter rolls, arbi tuk chat, OG pind chole bhature,rajma galouti wrap, bhutte ka khees served with khakhra, avo papdi chat, cappuccino,hot chocolate, raspberry matcha falooda, strawberry granola sundae, jalebi waffle, strawberry softserve and caramel icecream so far. Most of them were really good especially highlighting their chilli cheese toast,pav bhaji porter rolls, softserves, icecreams,sundae,coffees and jalebi waffle. Their salted caramel icecream served with their chocolate caramel barks is a must try. Personally found churros,hot chocolate to be too sweet for my liking. They do have a strawberry special menu for this season which is attached in the pics below. One cannot miss 'Bombay Sweet Shop' while visiting Phoenix palladium mall.

featured_reviews.name: Ragini Elf Gongo
featured_reviews.review_text:
I thought I couldn’t be more impressed by the Hunger Inc team… but today proved me wrong again!

I walked in with so many shopping bags, sweaty and awkward, because every table looked taken and my hands were hurting. Their team, not one but multiple people, instantly came forward to help with my bags and offered me a high seating table. Before anything else, he brought me a glass of water. I felt so cared for. And as a former hotelier, I can say this with confidence, this wasn’t an SOP, this was genuine hospitality.

Even during a busy service, the team took time to explain the dishes, check on me, and recommend what to try next.

I’ve always been a fan of Hunger Inc… and your success honestly feels personal to me.

Thank you!✨

featured_reviews.name: Amee Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay Sweet Shop hits a nerve.

Make mithai great again.
A line on a wall.
A promise on a plate.

The space pulls you back to Bombay sweet marts.
Metal tables with GM weight markers pressed into them.
The same tools once used to weigh barfis and pedas by hand.
You notice.
You pause.

Chit Chat on one side.
All wells that ends well on another.
Details matter here.

The food delivers.
Matar kachori with crisp bite and clean spice.
Lychee kombucha with balance and lift.
Both work together.

This works as a Starbucks replacement.
You sit.
You snack.
You stay longer.

In a world full of cupcakes be a laddo.
Bombay Sweet Shop lives by it.

description:
In the early forties, a young man from Braj in Mathura, landed on the shores of the bustling metropolis called Mumbai. He arrived with a dream to have his own shop selling traditional mithais from his beloved Braj Bhoomi. While he established his first outlet in Kalbadevi, little did he know that he was in fact pioneering a leading chain of stores which would one day become a household name! featured_reviews.review_text:
As one enters the shop everything looks very clean and organised. The staff is well trained in informing about their history, exchanging pleasantries and manages to put up a smile but what actually matters is their Mithais that they are selling which are not fresh!!!

This was the first time I bought an Ice Halwa, varieties of Pedas (white & brown) and some khakharas. They don't provide any sample tasting of their Mithais. Later upon the manager's intervention I was given a small sample of their brown peda which was fresh but not the other white peda or the Ice Halwa... I found that odd but went ahead on the trust of their rich legacy which was told to me by their staff... This was the first red flag.

Even though the staff knew that the sweets have gone stale they still sold it to me.  Upon tasting, I found out the truth about their stale mithai and also found out that they had not provided me with an invoice :-( Second red flag.

Now as I join the dots and it all makes sense that they probably have got good at clearing their stale products off the shelf and making money...
This was not experience that I had hoped for...

featured_reviews.name: Computer World
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent variety of genuine sweets.
Visited Zam Zam Sweets at Mohammed Ali Road and had a wonderful experience.

The food quality, taste, and freshness were excellent. Their sweets and snacks are absolutely delicious and full of authentic flavor. The staff was polite, service was quick, and the overall atmosphere was lively and enjoyable.

Definitely a must-visit place in Mumbai for anyone who loves good food and traditional sweets. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Ajay A
featured_reviews.review_text: I don't what's wrong with Zam zam sweets nowadays. I've purchased aflatoon and khaja from M A Ali Road but they provided stale sweets, which is not acceptable at all. Very disappointed this time.

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Mashelkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Opening during early hours at 9:00 AM, Zam Zam Sweets & Bakery serves a widevariety of toothsome treats, fresh from the oven. Known for being consistent with its quality as well as service, It is a great spot to visit in the company of colleagues to indulge in some office gossip and enjoy a variety of Bakery items....... it's best to visit the place during ramzaan.........

featured_reviews.name: Taaj Saifi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went there between 5 to 6 pm on 12/03/2025. The staff was very rude and not listening to anything I ordered malpua but they gave it to me folded in a foil paper with only a little mawa and two dips of milk It was not rabdi it was just liquid milk and there were no dry fruits
I told them that the last time I ordered it was packed in a box cut into pieces, and served with proper rabdi and dry fruits on top But the staff member replied rudely and said Madam if it is less then tell me how many you want  3 or 4
The staff behavior was very rude I would not recommend the Masjid Bunder Zam Zam to anyone You should go to another Zam Zam instead The staff there said Hum log aise hi dete hain

featured_reviews.name: Mohsin Khan
featured_reviews.review_text: *** My friend bought Diwali sweets for us on 24-10-22 and heres my personal experience. Firstly she had choosen Zam Zam Sweets over Trupti and Hasmukh because she feels that they sell the best sweets but that was not the case. I received stale sweets. Kadak Kaju Katli, Kadak Rose mithai like a rock. They have just spoiled the mood of Diwali sweets. She bought 5 kgs approx for all her friends and all of us experienced the same. "Band kardo bhai agar taazi mithai nahi bech sakte to" "Paiso ke chakkar me kisiki Diwali mat kharab karo" I will never recommend anyone to buy from this shop. 2stars only for Blueberry sweet which was atleast fresh ***

featured_reviews.name: Logical knowledge
featured_reviews.review_text: Zamzam is very famous Bakers shop in All-over Mumbai. There are many sweet and Bakers items. Sweet look like very fresh and testy. Staff behaviour is very good rates is very reasonable.

featured_reviews.review_text: Zam Zam sweets and bakeries located in Mohammad Ali road.. wide variety of sweets available..must try Aflatoon and anjeer sweet

featured_reviews.name: Sahil Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
My favourite bakery in Mumbai.
Every time I visit mumbai, i go to this bakery and buy at least a sweet, at least a cutless.

The taste this bakery gives is untouchable. The price is usually novelty but the product, the packaging, the quality is on point fr. So many varieties in sweet available there.

Always too crowded whenever i go there, it's one of the most popular sweet franchisees but obvious. No parking facility available there to be specific.

Try cutless, Rubber halwa and Aflatoon of this bakery. The bakery is worth it.
Attaching photos and videos for your reference.

featured_reviews.name: Kaustubh Deshpande
featured_reviews.review_text:
My family and I have been patrons of D Damodar for decades now. We really used to enjoy their sweets, particularly their barfis. But unfortunately, every business goes through cycles and post COVID, their food quality has dropped terribly. We recently purchased their rasgullas and rasmalais, but both of them weren't very good. It reflected a lack of care and desire to please their customers. The rasmalais(photos attached) were so bad that they couldn't even hold their shape, and were poorly flavored. As a customer, I felt let down.

Really hope things turn around for them and we can go back to enjoying their quality sweets again.  Sincerely rooting for them!

featured_reviews.name: Akshay S
featured_reviews.review_text: This is  very popular place in Dadar known not only for its sweets as the name suggests but also for it's snacks. I love their snacks, samosa, vada, sweet kachori, khandvi. The papaya chutney which they serve with the snacks is unique. Must try.

featured_reviews.name: ADITYA SALVI
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the oldest places in Dadar. Situated at the junction of Dadar TT. I feel it is an under-rated place. The food is good. I tried Vada, samosa, dhokla and Jalebi. I prefer all of it only when they serve it hot. Later on it doesn't taste that good. Hot samosa and chatni is a beautiful combination.

featured_reviews.name: Gurvinder Pal Singh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a very old establishment located at heart of Dadar TT. Though it is a shop for sweetmeats , my personal and childhood favourite here are the savouries such as Khandwi and Dhokla , lotus leaf dhokla and lastly the idli chutney . The khandwi beer is particularly good and highly recommended.

The shop provides good variety of sweets including Maharashtrian sweets like sutarfeni  ,different varieties of ladoos ,Punjabi sweets ,Bengali sweets .Mouth watering jalebi, Kachoris and samosa.

They keep good hygiene and have shops located at good localities where there is good facility for travel .
They have customized website and food on delivery options too.
